messages.author: 132678befc181647
messages.subject: Additive Effect Estimation with SG
parts:
Karl:

 

I would like to get your insight/comments on the estimation of additive effects in Rqtl when one has (like I do) a selectively genotyped (50 Highest / 50 Lowest Phenotype) plant population of 264 RILs. 

 

With SG you get purposeful (systematic) missing genotypes, as opposed to (say) random missing genotypes in a (mostly) fully genotyped population.  Multiple imputation is the obvious choice with the latter scenario, but what about  an SG scenario? 

 

The reason I ask this question is that I am now working with Rqtl commands to get additive effect estimates (and graphs thereof) of just the single (only) major QTL LOD score peak that I detected on Chr 7. 

 

Multiple imputation (via sim.geno) is automatically invoked in (most) of those Rqtl cmds (such as effectscan, effectplot, fitqtl) and result in AA : BB RIL means of 3.21 : 2.81 for the SNP tightly linked to this Chr 7 QTL.  The additive effect is estimated to be -0.17 using fitqtl with the parameter what=”draws”.  

 

Without imputation, the graph I get when  using the plot.pxg cmd (with the parameter infer=FALSE) displays SNP AA : BB means of 3.37 : 2.48, which would infer an additive effect of (3.37-2.48)/2= -0.44.  In fact, the estimate of -0.40 was obtained using fitqtl with the parameter what=”prob”, which is a Haley-Knott regression estimate, but does not HK perform poorly with missing data (as in an SG pop)?   

 

Is there an max likelihood (EM) option (with calc.prob) for computing additive effects in SG pops?  In any case, I would greatly appreciate your insight on the add effect estimate one should report when using SG. 

 

Thanks!

 

Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Additive Effect Estimation with SG
parts:
R/qtl doesn't currently have code to get MLEs of additive effects; only Haley-Knott regression or multiple imputation.

In the case of selective genotyping, Haley-Knott is really bad, so you're only option is imputation.
You want to be sure to include data on all phenotyped individuals and not just those with genotypes.

karl
